children: Chicago soybean and corn futures edged lower on Tuesday after investors trimmed bullish bets as harvesting advanced across the US Midwest and forecasts pointed to mostly favourable fieldwork weather this week.
Wheat futures followed corn and soybeans lower, despite ongoing concerns over Black Sea grain exports due to the Russia-Ukraine war.
FUNDAMENTALS
* The most-traded soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
fell 0.22% to $12.5-3/4 a bushel by 0052 GMT, touching an eight-week low.
* CBOT corn
slid 0.48% to $4.64-3/4 a bushel, its lowest level in more than two months, while wheat
fell 0.27% to $6.53-1/2 a bushel, hitting a more-than-two-month low.
* Scattered rains last week stalled field work in parts of the Midwest, but drier weather was expected through the end of the week, forecasters said.

* Harvest pressure outweighed support from renewed Chinese demand. The US Department of Agriculture on Monday confirmed private sales totalling 114,000 metric tons of US soybeans to China, bringing the confirmed sales total to China to 1.472 million tons over the past four days.
* US farmers harvested 64% of the soybean crop and 44% of the corn crop, according to the USDA's weekly crop progress report released on Monday. Both figures were below trade expectations
* Winter wheat planting was 63% complete, also below analysts' expectations of 65%.

* Russian wheat export prices eased slightly last week, while analysts raised their October export forecasts as shipments disrupted by the war with Ukraine are increasingly being redirected to Baltic terminals
* Commodity funds were net sellers of CBOT corn, soy and wheat, traders said on Monday (CBOT/FUNDS)
